name: The Dish It Kitchen
bio: Recipes tested on weeknights in a normal kitchen.

name: Bloom the spices
summary: Toast ground spices in hot fat for thirty seconds to wake up their oils.
detail: Warm oil or butter over medium heat, add the ground spices, and stir constantly until they smell nutty and darken a shade. Move quickly, since spices scorch in seconds and turn bitter.

name: Deglaze
summary: Add liquid to a hot pan and scrape up the browned bits for instant sauce.
detail: After searing, pour in stock, wine, or water while the pan is still hot. Scrape the base with a wooden spoon so the fond dissolves. That layer carries most of the roasted flavor.

name: Emulsify
summary: Whisk fat into liquid a little at a time so the dressing turns glossy and thick.
detail: Start with your acid, mustard, or egg yolk, then stream in the oil while whisking hard. Going slow at the start builds a stable base that will not split.

name: Rest the protein
summary: Let cooked meat sit off heat so the juices redistribute before slicing.
detail: Tent loosely with foil and wait five to fifteen minutes depending on size. Cutting too early lets the juice run onto the board instead of staying in each slice.

name: Blanch and shock
summary: Boil vegetables briefly, then plunge into ice water to lock in color and bite.
detail: Salt the water well, cook until just tender, then move straight to an ice bath. This stops the cooking and keeps greens vivid.

name: Fold
summary: Combine a light mixture into a heavier one without knocking out the air.
detail: Use a spatula to cut down through the center, sweep along the bowl, and turn over. Rotate the bowl a quarter turn and repeat until just combined.

name: Temper
summary: Raise the temperature of eggs or dairy slowly so they do not curdle.
detail: Whisk a ladle of the hot liquid into the eggs, then return the warmed mixture to the pot. Doing this in stages keeps the custard smooth.

name: Reduce
summary: Simmer a liquid so water evaporates and flavor plus body concentrate.
detail: Keep it at a steady simmer, not a hard boil, and watch the line on the side of the pan drop. A reduced sauce should coat the back of a spoon.

title: Weeknight Butter Chicken
intro: A faster take on the restaurant classic. The sauce leans on bloomed spices and a splash of cream rather than an overnight marinade, so it lands on the table in under an hour.
tips: No cream on hand works with full fat coconut milk, which nudges the dish dairy light.
Double the sauce and freeze half for an even faster round two.

steps.instruction: Toss the chicken with yogurt, garam masala, half the ginger, and half the garlic. Let it sit while you prep everything else.
Melt butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Add onion with a pinch of salt and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the remaining ginger and garlic, the paprika, and a spoon of garam masala. Bloom for thirty seconds until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes and sugar. Simmer until the sauce darkens and thickens, then blend smooth if you like a silky finish.
Slide in the chicken and its marinade. Cook gently until the pieces are just done.
Off the heat, swirl in the cream and taste for salt. Rest five minutes, then finish with coriander.

title: Charred Corn Elote Bowl
intro: Everything you love about street corn, loosened into a bowl you can eat with a spoon. Char the kernels hard so they keep a smoky bite under the dressing.
tips: Leftover bowl folds straight into scrambled eggs the next morning.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a cast iron pan until it shimmers. Add corn in one layer and leave it alone so it blisters.
Toss once, then char the second side. You want dark spots, not a full stir fry.
Whisk mayo, sour cream, lime juice and zest, and chili powder into a loose dressing.
Fold the warm corn into the dressing. Top with cotija, coriander, and jalapeno.

title: Miso Mushroom Ramen
intro: A weeknight broth that tastes long simmered thanks to roasted mushrooms and a spoonful of miso stirred in at the very end so it stays alive.
tips: Keep miso away from a hard boil or it loses its brightness and turns flat.

steps.instruction: Sear the mushrooms in sesame oil over high heat until deeply browned and shrunk by half.
Add garlic and ginger, cook one minute, then pour in the stock and soy. Simmer to build flavor.
Cook the noodles separately in salted water, then divide between bowls.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot broth until smooth, then stir it back into the pot off the heat.
Pour broth over the noodles and add your toppings.

title: Smoky Black Bean Tacos
intro: Pantry tacos with real depth. Chipotle and a squeeze of lime turn a can of beans into a filling nobody guesses was fifteen minutes of work.
tips: A crumble of cotija or a dollop of yogurt is welcome if you are not keeping it vegan.

steps.instruction: Soften the onion in olive oil, then add cumin and chipotle and stir until fragrant.
Add the beans with a splash of water. Simmer and mash a third of them for a creamy body.
Toss cabbage with lime juice and a pinch of salt for a quick slaw.
Char the tortillas over a flame or in a dry pan, then build with beans, slaw, and avocado.

title: Lemon Herb Roast Chicken
intro: The one recipe worth memorizing. A dry brine the night before is the only trick, and it turns an ordinary bird into something with shatteringly crisp skin.
tips: Save the carcass. Simmered with an onion and a carrot it becomes stock for the ramen above.

steps.instruction: The day before, pat the chicken dry and salt it all over. Rest uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Heat the oven to 220C. Stuff the cavity with lemon, garlic, and herbs, then rub the skin with oil.
Scatter potatoes around the bird. Roast until the thickest part of the thigh reads 74C.
Move the chicken to a board and rest it loosely tented while you crisp the potatoes in the drippings.
Carve and spoon the pan juices over the top.

title: Crispy Gnocchi with Sage Butter
intro: Skip the boiling water. Shelf stable gnocchi crisps up like a tiny potato roast straight in the pan, then gets tossed in nutty brown butter.
tips: A big handful of spinach wilted in at the end makes it feel like a full plate.

steps.instruction: Heat a dry nonstick pan, add gnocchi, and let them blister before tossing. They will puff slightly.
Add butter, sage, and garlic. Swirl until the butter foams, smells nutty, and turns amber.
Kill the heat, add a squeeze of lemon and the parmesan, and toss to coat.

title: One Pan Harissa Salmon
intro: A sheet pan dinner with a glaze that caramelizes at the edges. Chickpeas and tomatoes roast underneath and soak up everything that drips down.
tips: Firm white fish or thick tofu slabs take the same glaze and timing.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 210C. Toss chickpeas and tomatoes with oil and salt on a tray and roast for ten minutes.
Stir harissa with honey and a little oil. Coat the salmon fillets on all sides.
Nestle the salmon into the tray and roast until it flakes but is still glossy in the middle.
Finish with lemon, parsley, and a spoon of yogurt to cool the heat.

title: Silky Dal Tadka
intro: Comfort in a bowl. The lentils cook down until creamy, then a sizzling tadka of cumin, garlic, and chili gets poured over just before serving.
tips: A squeeze of lemon and a handful of coriander at the table keeps every bowl fresh.

steps.instruction: Simmer the lentils with tomato, turmeric, and plenty of water until they collapse into a loose puree.
Whisk to smooth it out and season with salt. Loosen with hot water if it tightens up.
In a small pan, heat the ghee and add cumin. When it sputters, add garlic and chili and fry until golden.
Take the tadka off the heat, stir in the chili powder, and pour the whole thing over the dal.

title: Salted Honey Olive Oil Cake
intro: Moist for days and barely sweet, this is the cake for people who say they do not like cake. A honey glaze soaks in while it is still warm.
tips: Use an olive oil you would happily drizzle on bread. The flavor carries straight through.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 175C and line a round tin. Whisk oil, sugar, and eggs until pale and thick.
Whisk in the milk and orange zest, then fold the flour and baking powder through in two additions.
Pour into the tin and bake until a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Warm the honey with a splash of water and brush it over the hot cake. Finish with flaky salt once cooled.

title: Dark Chocolate Tahini Cookies
intro: Fudgy in the center with a paper thin crackle on top. Tahini keeps them from being too rich and adds a savory hum you cannot quite place.
tips: Underbaking by a minute is the difference between a good cookie and a great one.

steps.instruction: Beat tahini, butter, and brown sugar until fluffy, then beat in the egg.
Fold in the flour, cocoa, and baking soda, then the chopped chocolate. Chill the dough.
Roll walnut sized balls in sesame seeds and space them well on lined trays.
Bake at 180C until the edges are set but the middles still look underdone. They firm as they cool.

title: No Churn Roasted Strawberry Ice Cream
intro: Roasting the berries first drives off water and concentrates their flavor, so the finished scoop tastes like summer even in January. No machine required.
tips: Freeze at least six hours. Overnight is better and it scoops cleanly after five minutes on the counter.

steps.instruction: Roast the strawberries with sugar at 200C until jammy and slightly caramelized, then cool and mash.
Whip the cold cream to firm peaks. In another bowl stir the condensed milk with lemon and salt.
Fold the cream into the condensed milk in three additions to keep it airy.
Ripple the strawberry through the base, freeze in a loaf tin, and cover the surface with parchment.

title: Peanut Butter Banana Recovery Shake
intro: The one to blend after a hard session. Real numbers on the protein, enough carbs to actually refuel, and it tastes like a milkshake you would order on purpose.
tips: Swap whey for a scoop of silken tofu and a date to keep it fully plant based.

steps.instruction: Add the oat milk first so the blades catch, then everything else on top.
Blend on high until completely smooth and the ice is gone, about forty seconds.
Pour into a cold glass. Streak the inside with extra peanut butter first if you want the diner look.

title: Green Glow Pineapple Shake
intro: Bright, not grassy. Pineapple and lime do the heavy lifting so the spinach just rides along for the color and the iron.
tips: Freeze leftover shake in a lolly mould for a two ingredient feeling dessert.

steps.instruction: Blend the spinach with the coconut water first until no flecks remain.
Add the frozen fruit, lime, and ginger and blend again until thick and pourable.
Taste and adjust with more lime for zip or banana for body.

title: Cold Brew Coffee Malt
intro: A grown up malted shake. Cold brew keeps it from being cloying and the malt powder gives that old soda fountain roundness.
tips: No malt powder means a fine classic coffee shake. It is not the same, but nobody complains.

steps.instruction: Blend everything except the whipped cream in short pulses so it stays thick.
Check the texture. It should be spoonable at first and drinkable after a minute.
Pour into chilled glasses and top with whipped cream and a dusting of extra malt.

title: Hibiscus Ginger Cooler
intro: Tart, floral, and the most striking color in the fridge. Brew it strong, sweeten lightly, and let everyone cut it with soda to taste.
tips: The spent flowers are not trash. Chop and simmer with sugar for a quick jammy topping.

steps.instruction: Simmer the hibiscus and ginger in the water for ten minutes, then take it off the heat.
Stir in the sweetener while warm so it dissolves, then steep another ten minutes.
Strain and chill. Add lime juice once cold so it stays bright.
Serve over ice, half concentrate and half soda, with a slap of mint.

title: Cucumber Mint Agua Fresca
intro: The most refreshing thing you can make in five minutes. Blend, strain, chill. It tastes like the inside of a cucumber, in the best way.
tips: Leave the skin on one cucumber for a greener color and a little more structure.

steps.instruction: Blend the cucumber with the water and mint until completely liquid.
Strain through a sieve, pressing the solids to get every drop.
Stir in lime, sweetener, and a tiny pinch of salt to make the flavor pop. Chill well.

title: Spiced Golden Milk
intro: A bedtime mug that actually earns its place. Simmering the spices in fat, then whisking hard, is what turns this from dusty to silky.
tips: The pinch of pepper is not optional. It is what makes the turmeric actually do something.

steps.instruction: Warm the fat in a small pot and add the turmeric, cinnamon, pepper, and ginger. Stir for thirty seconds.
Pour in the milk and bring to a bare simmer, whisking so nothing catches.
Whisk hard for a full minute to froth it, then sweeten off the heat and strain into mugs.
